description: The Clean Watersheds Needs Survey is EPA's periodic inventory of US clean water infrastructure and of the capital investment needed over the next 20 years to meet Clean Water Act goals. The 2022 survey, the 17th since 1972 and the first with all states and territories taking part, reports $630.1 billion of needs as of 1 January 2022: $345.7 billion for wastewater (over 40 per cent for pipes and pump stations), $115.3 billion for stormwater, $94.4 billion for nonpoint source control and $74.7 billion for decentralized treatment. It also records technical data on 17,544 publicly owned treatment works serving 270.4 million people, including flows, population served, discharge, effluent and unit processes. EPA prepared it as a Report to Congress under Clean Water Act sections 516 and 609, for projects eligible for State Revolving Fund loans. Coverage is national, at facility and project level, with state totals. Access: a free dashboard with national or state downloads as CSV or an Access database plus data dictionary, report PDFs, and earlier cycles; a HydroShare compilation gives 1984 to 2022 as CSV. Caveats: the survey is voluntary and EPA says the total likely underestimates true need; some costs come from EPA cost estimation tools. Simulation uses: sizing and locating wastewater and stormwater assets, investment and adaptation planning, and ageing-infrastructure scenarios. Related records: HydroWASTE (data-hydrowaste), the European UWWTD plant data (data-uwwtd-treatment-plants) and England's storm overflow returns (data-ea-edm-storm-overflows-annual-returns).
